title: Luca Van Assche Faces Rinky Hijikata After Reaching First Masters 1000 Quarterfinal

 Luca V an Assche reached his first ATP Masters 1000 quarterfinal at the 2026 Paris Masters after beating Learner Tien and Lorenzo Musetti, setting up a clash with Rinky Hijikata.
 by Sportscape Editor | Nov 06, 2026 | 2 minute read Luca Van Assche celebrates reaching his first Masters 1000 quarterfinal at the Paris Masters, where he will face Rinky Hijikata after reflecting on his career struggles and coaching improvements. · Credits; Via ATP Tennis Luca Van Assche is enjoying an important week at the 2026 Paris Masters after reaching his first ATP Masters 1000 quarter-final. The Frenchman defeated American Learner Tien and Italian Lorenzo Musetti to book his place in the last eight. He will now face Australia’s Rinky Hijikata on Centre Court as he looks to continue his impressive run. Van Assche, who is the last French player remaining in the tournament, also spoke to L’Équipe about his childhood dream, the difficult period he faced last year and how he has improved his game with coach Sébastien Villette.
 Van Assche Recalls His Childhood Dream and Difficult Period
 Van Assche was especially happy to reach the main court in Paris because he used to watch tennis there as a child. Playing at the same venue as a professional is a special moment for him.
 “It’s an incredible feeling. For a long time, I dreamed of playing on center court at Bercy, where I often went as a kid as a spectator.
 “It’s true that I’ve won a lot this year. I gained a lot of confidence. I also improved a lot. I’m very happy with the way my game is evolving,” Van Assche told L’Équipe.
 The 21-year-old also opened up about the difficult time he experienced after breaking into the top 100 at 19. He was not used to losing so often, and returning to the Challenger Tour was not easy for him.
 “These are certainly not easy periods. Especially because I was always used to not really facing difficulties. I broke into the top 100 at 19... There were doubts, I asked myself questions about what I wanted to do.
 “I went back to the Challenger circuit, where the level is very high. And I wasn’t winning much. Naturally, I took it badly. Winning the Olbia Challenger did me a lot of good.
 “It also allowed me to regain confidence and build on a good start to the season. I realized that I loved tennis. I just also needed to like the way I play.”
 Coach Helps Van Assche Change His Approach
 Van Assche also explained how working with Villette since the start of the year has helped him. He said their understanding developed quickly and that his coach's strict approach gave him confidence.
 “We started working with Sébastien at the beginning of the year. We understood each other very well, quickly. He’s someone who is very strict and who has a lot of confidence in me.
 “What I learned a lot with him was about the mental side. There are a lot of players and people who emphasize the mental side as the most important thing. That’s what I did too before I met him.
 “But in the end, tennis is really a racket sport where you hit a ball. We needed to take some of the drama out of all that. I attached a lot of importance to it; I blamed a lot of defeats on mentality.”
 Now, Van Assche faces another big test against Hijikata. He knows the Australian has earned his place in the quarter-finals after beating Novak Djokovic at the tournament. He also understands that Hijikata’s fast and aggressive style will make the match difficult.
 “It’s going to be another good match against an excellent player. If he’s in the quarterfinals, it’s because he deserves his place. He beat Djokovic here... It’s also a surface that suits him well. He plays fast, tense tennis. It’s going to be another good fight.”
